rules.title: Source-of-lawful-income housing discrimination ban (NJ Law Against Discrimination)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not refuse to rent, deny availability, or otherwise discriminate against a tenant or purchaser based on the lawful source of income or lawful source of rent/mortgage payment they use — for example, a landlord cannot deny a lawful Section 8 HUD voucher holder the right to rent an apartment based solely on that source of income.

coverage_conditions.notes: Also exempt: rental of a room or rooms within a one-family dwelling occupied by the owner/occupant as their residence at the time of the rental.

rules.exemptions: The LAD's housing provisions (including the source-of-income protection) do not apply to: rental of a single apartment/flat in a two-family dwelling where the other unit is owner-occupied at the time of rental; rental of a room or rooms within a one-family dwelling occupied by the owner/occupant as their residence; preference given to persons of the same religion by a religious organization in sale, lease or rental; and (for the familial-status protection specifically) housing for older persons as defined at N.J.S.A. 10:5-5mm.
rules.interaction: Enforced by the NJ Division on Civil Rights; a complaint may be filed with the Division within 180 days of the alleged violation, or in NJ Superior Court within two years. The Division does not handle ordinary landlord-tenant disputes concerning evictions.
rules.quoted_span:
The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based
on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent
or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses.
rules.conflict_note: Document (an NJ AG/Division on Civil Rights consumer brochure) does not itself cite a section number for the source-of-income provision beyond naming the 'LAD'; N.J.S.A. 10:5-12 is the standard housing-discrimination section of the Law Against Discrimination and is inferred, not quoted verbatim in the text.
